label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 3 pilot (live recorded window), not the evaluation

report.summary: Notifications were delayed by an outbox backlog: publications fell below arrivals for about 2 minutes, and the delay coincided with a slow consumer handler (~405 ms). No delivery failures. The serialized-publisher link is inferred.

findings.claim: The outbox fell behind: arrivals held at 32 per 10 s while publications dropped to about 18-19 per 10 s, so pending grew to 124 and oldest age to 38.5 s.
findings.reason: Per-bucket counts and the pending and oldest-age samples show the backlog building, then draining in a burst.

findings.claim: The transfer API was healthy: all 477 requests returned 201 with p99 of 0.25 s. The delay is downstream of the request path.
findings.reason: The API shows no errors or slowness, while the outbox shows the lag.

findings.claim: Attempts did not fail; they were slow. Latency was bimodal (p50 72 ms, p95 481 ms), and the slow part was consumer handler time (p95 405 ms vs p50 0.03 ms).
findings.reason: All 478 attempts succeeded on attempt 1, and the extra latency is attributed to the consumer handler, not auth or network.

findings.claim: Slow handler responses likely throttled a serial publisher to about 2 per second, below the 3.2/s arrival rate, which produced the backlog.
findings.reason: About 19 per 10 s matches roughly 480 ms per attempt run serially; publisher concurrency was not observed.

alternatives.hypothesis: Publisher polling or batching stalled for a reason unrelated to consumer latency.
alternatives.reason: The publication rate matches the slow-attempt duration, and the burst that cleared the backlog came with no failures.

alternatives.hypothesis: Retries or failures caused the delay.
alternatives.reason: Failed was 0 throughout, and every attempt succeeded on attempt 1.

limitations: Publisher concurrency and poll-batch configuration were not observed, so the serialization mechanism is unconfirmed.
Only the earliest 100 of 478 delivery log rows are listed; the aggregates cover all of them. The consumer is a test fixture, which may not reflect real consumer behavior.
next_checks: Check the publisher's concurrency and batch size, and whether it waits on each consumer response before sending the next.
Find why the consumer handler took about 405 ms during the slow period, and when that slowness started and stopped.

report.summary: Outbox publication lagged arrivals mid-window (pending up to 124, oldest age 38s) and later caught up. No failures. Slow consumer handler deliveries are the likely drain bottleneck.

findings.claim: Outbox backlog built up mid-window: publications ~18-19 per 10s vs 32 arrivals, then a catch-up burst of 77/80/61.
findings.reason: Per-bucket counts show a sustained shortfall, pending rose to 124 and oldest undelivered age to 38.5s, then drained.

findings.claim: The transfers API and delivery outcomes were healthy: all 201s, all attempts succeeded on first try, with no auth, network or server errors.
findings.reason: Request errors 0, delivery logs 478/478 success, failed gauge 0. Delay is queueing, not failure or retry.

findings.claim: Some deliveries were slow because of consumer handler time (p95 405ms vs p50 0.03ms), which likely throttled serial drain and caused the lag.
findings.reason: Total p95 481ms matches handler p95 plus ~71ms auth; a slow tail fits the reduced publication rate, but timing per bucket was not correlated.

limitations: Delivery logs list only the earliest 30 of 478 records, so slow deliveries cannot be placed in time against the backlog window.
Pending is a gauge sampled at scrape times; the cause of the consumer handler slowness is not visible.
next_checks: Align slow consumer handler timings with the 09:46:50-09:48:40 backlog window, for example by listing delivery logs with timestamps beyond the first 30.
Inspect outbox poller batch size, interval and concurrency, and consumer handler logs, for the mid-window slowdown.

alternatives.reason: No poller or batch-level data was inspected; the consumer slowness correlation is not time-aligned.
alternatives.hypothesis: Outbox poller or worker stalled or throttled independently of the consumer (e.g. batch or interval change).

alternatives.reason: Arrivals were constant at 32 per 10s and the API latency was stable.
alternatives.hypothesis: Transfer ingestion load caused the backlog.
